prompt: A coil of 200 turns experiences a change in magnetic flux from 0.08 Wb to 0.02 Wb in 0.10 s. Calculate the induced emf.
explanation: Faraday's law, size first. The CHANGE in flux is 0.08 − 0.02 = 0.06 Wb, and it happens in 0.10 s, so the rate of change is 0.06 / 0.10 = 0.6 Wb per second. Multiply by the 200 turns: emf = N x rate = 200 x 0.6 = 120 V. Two traps live here. The flux VALUES do not go into the formula, only their difference. And the number of turns multiplies, because each turn is its own loop cut by the same changing flux.

why.a: Correct. 200 turns times a rate of 0.6 Wb per second.
why.b: Wrong by a factor of ten in the division by 0.10 s.
why.c: Wrong. 0.6 V is the rate of change of flux, before multiplying by the 200 turns.
why.d: Wrong. 200 is the number of turns, not a voltage.
why.e: Wrong. This uses a flux change of 0.01 Wb rather than 0.06 Wb.
